# Additive tuning of 2026-11-08, mcp round 2 confirmation, scenario 5

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5
tree: sha256:a7bde7d037f359894dc19c4a6c209888291ec5716ca604a048b513eb82768c69
lock: sha256:826dcf9f83c5d9e7fb557d7a1df9753a09a5c70c645d6c9faf7a575256119178
selection: sha256:d99530b2b639bb6bdd279be2a9356a64ce2a0c8cceca354d56957f198a76a20a
read_set: sha256:2a47d5b0401ca6d3239d352781fe101f4d7ba74c60c6a0dbe460e46ae9703c4d
seed: 0
harness: 0.6.1
tier: additive
arm: scenario-5
at: 2026-11-07
```

**This line is the confirmation of round 2 of the MCP layer, in the tuning round of the additive campaign that [#1880](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880) asked for.** The owner opened round 2 to turn the use of the tools into correct answers, and not into more use ([comment 6701580649](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880#issuecomment-6701580649)). The round screened variants 1, 2 and 4 at 22 sessions each, and the owner voided variant 3 after its canary. The owner ruled that the round ranks on passes, with a tie going to the lower cost ([comment 6712870651](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880#issuecomment-6712870651) and [comment 6713732364](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880#issuecomment-6713732364)). Variant 2 ranked first, with 18 of 22 passed at 1727 cents ([the screen of variant 2](additive-tuning-of-2026-11-07-mcp-round-2-variant-2-scenario-5.md)). The confirmation runs that variant again at 154 sessions, against the best so far measured at the same count. Variant 2 makes the `check` tool read the tree as it is now and puts the files changed since the server started first. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-5 tuning`, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288.

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `8c7b393d`, on the pushed branch `tune/mcp-r2-v2`, for the whole batch, and it is the commit the screen of variant 2 ran at. The `try.sh` of `main` at `3d5ca2f8` (#1940) ran the launch, the relaunch and the result, because the pinned branch does not carry the ruling on rank. The base it is read against is scenario 2 at `329f3362`, and the owner accepted the change to the MCP server against that base ([comment 6656833861](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880#issuecomment-6656833861)). The canary of 8 sessions cost 651 cents, and the owner read its records and [passed it](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880#issuecomment-6717982959). The driver then halted six times at 126 of 154 sessions, when the plan's session limit stopped the harness. It continued after the limit reset, in the same try root at the same pin.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 154 sessions and cost 13288 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 3 stopped at the turn cap, 2 stopped at the session budget, 108 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. 102 of the 154 sessions used the MCP layer, against 101 of 154 in the best so far. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 5 with variant 2 passed 122 of the 154 sessions it graded, 79%. The keep row compares this line with the best so far of the layer, which passed 116 of 154 ([the best so far](additive-tuning-of-2026-11-06-mcp-round-1-best-so-far-scenario-5.md)). The difference is +3.9 points, with the interval [-5.5, +13.2]. The interval includes zero, so the change is not kept under the owner's rule of 2026-10-20 (#1777, ruling 7). The base row compares this line with the base, scenario 2, which passed 112 of 154 ([the base](additive-tuning-of-2026-11-02-engine-round-1-best-so-far-scenario-2.md)): +6.5 points, with the interval [-3.1, +15.9]. `try.sh result` closed round 2 of the MCP layer as not kept, and the best so far at `cce750f7` stays the layer's best so far. The use of the layer did not rise, and the passes rose by an amount that this batch cannot tell from chance.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,300.00 for this layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 20000 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 13436 cents against its cap. The 154 recorded sessions account for 13288 cents, the 651 cents of the canary included. The other 148 cents are the partial cost of the sessions that the halts stopped, which the driver recorded again. A confirmation is charged to the tuning ceiling, which now holds 43308 of 100000 cents.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1880/mcp-r2-confirm/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.

not part of common abbreviations, followed by space+capital or end\\n    text = block.strip()\\n    if not text:\\n        return 0\\n    # remove common abbreviations to avoid false splits\\n    abbr = re.sub(r'\\\\b(e\\\\.g|i\\\\.e|etc|vs|cf|U\\\\.S|Mr|Mrs|Dr|Ms|Jr|St|No)\\\\.', lambda m: m.group(0).replace('.', '@'), text)\\n    count = 0\\n    for m in re.finditer(r'[.!?]+', abbr):\\n        count += 1\\n    return count\\n\\nresults = []\\nfor f in files:\\n    with open(f, encoding='utf-8') as fh:\\n        content = fh.read()\\n    # split into blocks: blank-line separated paragraphs, and within those, list items split by lines starting with -,*,+,digit.\\n    paragraphs = re.split(r'\\\\n\\\\s*\\\\n', content)\\n    for p in paragraphs:\\n        lines = p.split('\\\\n')\\n        # group list items: a line starting with a bullet/number starts a new block; continuation lines (indented, no bullet) belong to it\\n        blocks = []\\n        cur = []\\n        for line in lines:\\n            if re.match(r'^\\\\s*([-*+]|\\\\d+\\\\.)\\\\s+', line):\\n                if cur:\\n                    blocks.append('\\\\n'.join(cur))\\n                cur = [line]\\n            elif re.match(r'^#', line) or line.strip()=='' :\\n                if cur:\\n                    blocks.append('\\\\n'.join(cur))\\n                cur = []\\n            else:\\n                cur.append(line)\\n        if cur:\\n            blocks.append('\\\\n'.join(cur))\\n        for b in blocks:\\n            if re.match(r'^\\\\s*(```|#|\\\\|)', b):\\n                continue\\n            c = count_sentences(b)\\n            if c > 6:\\n                results.append((f, c, b[:200]))\\n\\nfor r in results:\\n    print(r[0], r[1])\\n    print(r[2])\\n    print('---')\\nprint(\\\"TOTAL FLAGGED:\\\", len(results))\\nEOF\",\"description\":\"Scan markdown fixtures for paragraphs/items with >6 sentences\"}"
